definitions.explanation: Doing something without difficulty or strain, in a relaxed and comfortable manner.

examples.japanese: {楽々|らくらく}と{持|も}ち{上|あ}げた。
この{椅子|いす}は{座|すわ}り{心地|ごこち}がよくて、{楽々|らくらく}{作業|さぎょう}できる。
examples.english: This chair is comfortable and makes it easy to work.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいソフトを{使|つか}えば、{複雑|ふくざつ}なデータ{処理|しょり}も{楽々|らくらく}こなせるようになった。
examples.english: With the new software, even complex data processing can be handled with ease.

notes:
A reduplication of {楽|らく} (easy, comfortable). Functions as an adverb, often followed by と ({楽々|らくらく}と). Conveys a sense of performing a task without visible effort or strain.

USAGE:
Commonly used in product marketing and advertising to emphasize ease of use (e.g., {楽々|らくらく}{操作|そうさ} "easy operation"). Also appears in brand names.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {楽々|らくらく}と{運|はこ}ぶ: to carry easily
- {楽々|らくらく}{操作|そうさ}: easy operation
- {楽々|らくらく}クリア: easily cleared/completed
- {楽々|らくらく}{収納|しゅうのう}: easy storage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {簡単|かんたん}に: simply, easily — more neutral and objective
- すらすら: smoothly, fluently — specifically for smooth, uninterrupted flow (reading, speaking)
- {難|なん}なく: without difficulty — slightly more formal
